[spoiler=[b]Starbound RP: First Strike
Federation - Korrin War[/b]]

[b]February 27th 2167 - Erene sphere - Lagrange 5 - Side 10 [/b]

Vissarius left Korrin with a vanguard fleet comprised of his destroyer, two frigates, and a corvette. With the help of a Comet-class corvette, Vissarius' fleet managed to evade detection by any distant ships passing through the Belt of Tears, hunting down two trade ships that were struggling to navigate the belt. He made his way undetected to Mastodon to resupply and then sped towards Dupont. His fleet hid in Dupont's Kartovsky Range, attacking isolated trade ships, which now rose to 7 destroyed vessels as he awaited an opportunity...

[i]"Beautiful isn't it?" [/i]Vissarius said calmly, his eyes fixated on Erene as he gazed deeply at the world from the command room of his destroyer. From his distance it seemed like a blue ball, with patches of white clouds like small pieces of wool across its smooth surface, while the lights on the night of the world were a dazzling display.

[i]"It's beautiful, but...I can never bring myself to love it. It's as distant to me as the moons of Hyperborea; it's a stranger I could never have a connection with, even if I marvel at its majesty."[/i] In his hand Vissarius held his black tinted glasses, having taken them off to appreciate the colours of Erene with his very own eyes. As he stared at Erene, his eyes drifted to the nearby space colonies, a cluster of cylinders drifting in the vacuum of space.

[i]"I can never love Erene; it is dotted with reminders of its exploitation of the home of my people. Those colonies were made from the resources of Spacenoids, all our work taken to benefit this dying planet..."[/i] Vissarius looked back at Erene and at the southern pole where the blue waters met with the red of the Dead Ocean, then he quickly turned his head to the colonies.[i] "Unfortunate for the people of those colonies, caught between Korrin's fight for independence and the Federation's greed to stay in control of Spacenoid exploitation. Whatever happens now is because of the corruption of the Erene Federation..."[/i]

Vissarius smirked, closing his eyes for a moment as he relished in the opportunity to fight. [i]"Our resources built these colonies. If the Federation wants the resources so bad, why don't we send some their way, down to earth." [/i]Vissarius' smirk grew into a grin; he stepped back and pointed at the closest colony to his fleet, a cylinder named Azure Lake. [i]"Deploy every mobile suit and have them advance ahead of the fleet, they'll have to destroy any Federation ship they see while ours get in range. Once the fleet is in position, fire on the colony and target their propellant. Be precise and watch your fire to not hit the advance force. Everyone, to battle stations, condition 1!"[/i]

An alarm blared throughout the destroyer as the crew prepared for battle, officers rushing to their seats while the mechanics finished any work they did on the mobile suits before sending them off. Vissarius put on his tinted glasses and casually walked to his commander, placing his hand on his shoulder. [i]"Azel, you're in charge of the fleet while I'm gone. I'll be getting in my mobile suit."[/i] Commander Azel nodded and saluted Vissarius as he walked away. [i]"Yes, captain! Glory to you in battle!"[/i]

Vissarius personally led the advance force, which consisted of 8 mobile suits calibrated towards space combat, while Commander Azel led the ships. The fleet's particle guns were not yet in range, but an initial barrage of medium and heavy missiles was fired towards the cylinder, some missing while most struck at the hulls and windows of Azure Lake. Most of the damage did not go through the thick walls of the colony, but large underground utility areas were destroyed, and essential systems were crippled in the barrage.

The colony couldn't detect the fleet until they entered visual range, as they managed to use the Kartovsky Range of Dupont and Erene to stay hidden, though once they did, a full evacuation was ordered as the civilians were rushed into shelters or into escape ships as a distress message began to be sent across the Erene sphere:

[i][b]"We are under attack! This is the Azure Lake colony and we are under attack! Ships bearing the symbols of Korrin have been spotted coming from Dupont. We repeat, we have spotted ships bearing the symbols of Korrin. We are requesting all available Federation forces to assist us! We are under attack; please send help!"[/b][/i][/spoiler]

[spoiler=Lockheed News

Erene 2000 RP][i]The Military Defence Institute (MDI) after operational testing has approved the usage of The FTO-640 clip on thermal optics in operational service. They won't be replacing the dual band thermals used by the infantry as they are more powerful and better in almost all scenarios for detection and engagement in conventional conflict except following scenarios which require fast reaction CQB, urban stuff and police work. Now units can instead also request to get clip on thermals when in an CQB environment to cover any photonic barriers and dark spots where the night vision can't cover and IR lights are too risky to use in peer to peer conflict. Domestic law enforcement units that operate in CQB work like hostage rescue have also been issued the FTO-640 clip on thermals.

United States of Lockheed recently made a deal with Neue Republik for the sale of providing and integration the IGAS receiver for Anti Jamming GPS capabilities in their military's precision guided munitions and missiles.

The receiver developed by DIG systems the biggest missile manufacturer of USL utilizes 24 channel dual frequency all in view navigation. Based on the field tested old 12-channel JDAMs receiver and offering more channels than any other available receiver in the world for countering and protection against electronic warfare systems in the evolving ECM race and precision strikes in those environments. It will provide all precision guided munitions with benefits with the Quinksink and Anti Radiation missiles getting the most increase to their usage effectiveness. Also the dark factories for the receiver would allow for faster integration of the system in all Neue Republik current and future munitions.

Further the Lockheed Aviation force in a deal will be permanently stationing 7 aerial tankers and 2 Airborne Early Warning and control aircraft in Union of Avalon and sale of 2 AEW&C aircraft to allow the allied nation's airforce aerial refueling capability and access to the newest AESA radar, mesh communications, missile, tactical and theatre datalinks of the AEW&Cs. 

DIG systems will be also building dark factories in Qartena Hadasht which will be used to increase the production of precision guided munitions and help with lowering prices from economies of scale.

The MDI has also in an recent audit of the ground forces found that it's logistics vehicles are now hovering around 45% a decrease due to increase in other vehicles and following it have ordered a plan qnd boost to production lines of logistics vehicles to increase the number upto 30,000 from 20,000 to keep balance of vehicles ratio.
[/i][/spoiler]

[spoiler=Bob related news][i] Recently in the parliament the issue of Bobian West and North Elseyr was raised again with representative Gary W Bush saying "Why do we tolerate the existence of Bobian West and North Elseyr. They are harbouring weapons of mass destruction near us. The people confused about their own identities with them being spread on islands continents apart. We must unite everyone there under an unified singular identity the Lockheed identity."

Later the entire government seems to have been confirmed to be following the narrative for a while with the updated mal released showing even a few more Bobian smaller islands not just the major big islands this time shown under United States of Lockheed adminstration.

There has also been more than just words used for saber rattling this time. With Lockheed showing off the world's first Stealth UCAVs in the world in operational service with no other nation having to it's equivalent by having it and a few MC-30A conduct a flight to show it over and violating Bobian airspace in sorties to show Bobian leadership that Lockheed has technology capable of crippling their military's fighting capacity. There are also been incidents of patrol ships entering Bobian waters and using water hose on any thing deemed unauthorised personnel mainly Bobian fishermen on charges of getting too close to the military vessel after even multiple warnings and not giving them passage of way being a potential threat to the ship as they could carry a hidden explosive to get near the ship. 

United States of Lockheed have also announced a massive multiple joint Naval force and Aviation force joint drills which would go around and just outside Bobian waters which are being done to show that the Lockheed military can effectively encircle the islands if an actual war were to start. The drills are expected to begin on 26 th May  and affected areas will have a notice issued to them about the drills to avoid any unauthorised personnel from entering the area where drills will be conducting.

[/i][/spoiler]

The world has suffered changes since its very beginning, whether it's a rock falling from a treetop or the shifting of continental plates; things have undeniably been different at several points of time. The same can be said of segments of Erene, whose territories' ecosystems, landscapes and so on have been completely modified by the planet's intelligent species. There is one area, though, which is notorious for its difficulty to face change due to its renowned inherent challenges in terms of livability.

Antipodea, the southern continent. While it has a couple of colonies on its lands, it's yet known as a bastion of natural purity and minimal exploitation, sparse settlements and alike. That unique quality is what defines the continent, but there is one major exception, even if it doesn't find itself on the mainland.

Banhockia is a small nation comprised of roughly one-hundred and fourty thousand people, but one with an infamous particularity; until 2004, the entirety of the nation's territory lay on an archipelago of roughly 7 major landmasses, whose main attraction is the one, eternal ruler of the isles: the cold. Excluding the most populated island of Marmella, essentially the whole country finds itself below the 66th parallel; in essence, making Banhockia the only Antipodea-based nation in Erene.

While the weather and typical conditions are nothing to marvel at, there is certainly a sense of pride among the nation's people, which stretches back to their origins from the 15th century, when a small Hayan-Dalian expedition of five ships (represented in Banhockia's flag) landed on modern-day Amagalde island, the second-most inhabited territory in Banhockia. Scriptures of the time written by Galorilist scholars, who found themselves as a semi-religious authority looking to reestablish order, described the feelings amongst the 550 or so people who were unfortunate enough to land on this rough wasteland in the middle of local autumn: [i]"The families which sought lives like those of the elites, vacationing and acquiring gifts and souvenirs from foreign lands, they were also looking for something of a new life. Their dirty farms and unexciting adventures weren't very palpable, and as such, many of them of varying sizes accompanied the explorers on their trip. At this point, it's more desirable to drag yourself through pigs' droppings than having to search for unfrozen, fresh water."[/i]

The sentiment which echoed through the populace was one of despair, and it is likely that at least a sixth of the population, including children, died within the first month of settlement, as the aforementioned documents have recounted. The first newborn in the society wouldn't arrive until the fourth month after the discovery of the isles. Either way, the marooned expedition almost immediately got to work to fix the issues. While the initial landing on Amagalde's shores was tricky, the boats used to navigate to it were repaired relatively quickly from our understanding, since, not long after the first isle was found, a second was encountered, modern-day Bemetha island, the location of Banhockia's current capital, eponymous to the landmass it sits on. Hastily, the minority aristocracy took advantage and set up a stone fort on the island, secluding itself from the rest, intending to impose a similar rule to the one back home.

The story of the first year of Banhockia has been studied endlessly by economists, psychologists and alike, as they tried to comprehend how the minute group of people that originally stumbled upon the island managed to dig themselves out of the rut they'd fallen into, but also how a local system of governance was so quickly enabled, even if unwillingly by most of the people involved in the new society, and the way that, despite the likely disillusionment with the establishment, people fell back in line so quickly. Currency was more valuable as a commodity than as an economic tool; services were unable to simply be sold, for nothing was worth the work nor was there enough time for most to assist others. Individualism reigned for a moment, and as much as the newly formed government's intervention may have calmed this, the problems persisted.

Documentation of the events were mostly from elitist perspectives, and modern historians notice an elevated distaste towards the majority as time and society progressed, sensing their grip loosening simultaneous to the expansion of towns. The majority, living in a couple of isolated communities in Amalgade and later Marmella, were largely disconnected from the administration, and as such, their lives were generally a lot less restricted; even with the contemporary conditions. Despite this meaning that the relationship between the government and its people was strained, the villages that sprung up in the meantime, probably consisting of some 50 people each, effectively collaborated with each other to make efficient transport networks (mainly on the northern seaboard), island-spanning guilds and small and unappealing, yet existing and useful living spaces in the westerly hills of the island, protecting from the strong winds in the upcoming winter.

A year after the arrival of the expedition, a census was carried out and determined that there were now 496 people in the islands. This statistic came prior to a population increase caused by the discovery of Marmella, allowing the planting of some crops and thus providing nourishment to a larger sector of the population, allowing the production of many offspring. Lots of the newborns died in their infancy, as the third-year census, in 1569, counted 773 people in total. It is very possible that many more babies had been born in the previous two years, but simply died due to the tenuous situation.

Once the populace on Marmella began to develop the island, the government, now led by Halga Masoro as "Supreme Councilor", sought to move their operations to the island, as its wealth-retaining, authoritative status waned with the effectively complete abandonment of currency and overall independence of the people. However, once the administration seized properties at the source and mouth of the Caeselga river (Marmella's main, transversal waterway), taking control of its valuable waters, not using a justification other than [i]"the necessity of egalitarian distribution of aliment"[/i] (Javai Soungre, 1571) there was an immediate sense of distrust cultivated between it and its subjects. As such, in 1574, when the government had begun to build a settlement, fully purposed for its own needs, utilizing much of the valuable material found throughout the waterway, a revolt was staged by enraged civilians who assassinated and kidnapped several politicians. A year later, the construction was completed and the authoritarian regime was fully ousted and replaced by a rotational system, whereby a council made up of guild leaders from every town (of which there were ~6 major ones by this point, major meaning >100 people) would decide on one guild leader (not necessarily in the council) to be the main administrator for one year. The council was refreshed every 2 years, in a selection that was done by local town councils, which would be the main providers of services, a concept truly reintroduced to the economy only after the disappearance of the previous government.

By 1600, with yearly census, there were around 2500 people on the islands. By this point, 6 of the landmasses had been found, the previously named ones alongside Taakarsu island and the Jorabore isles. The final island to be found, Ermanban, the southernmost and third-least populated today, was discovered in 1618, quite a while after the original arrival on the Banhock archipelago.

Each of the isles now plays a role in the Banhockia, now a presidential republic. Marmella, outside of being the main population center with the two most populated cities, is also the produce and trading capital of the nation. Sitting on it are the cities of Deumibla and Enmanhol, the former being larger due to its location, providing it with clean water and better soil, while Enmanhol became the commerce and financial hub, housing many flourishing businesses and the largest port in the nation. Marmella is also the most tourism-friendly spot, with great scenery at almost any time of year.

The first of all of them to be discovered, Amalgade, is undoubtedly the best site for history in the nation. The oldest remnants of the oldest times of Banhockia, while also thriving due to its rare platinum and quartz variants, which is later used elsewhere in the country to produce technological devices and more. Amalgade's largest city is Mesaega, the third-largest in Banhockia.

Bemetha is largely still the capital's island. No other cities exist on it, and the capital itself only has about 1 thousand people on it, mostly civil servants. The fort which the capital is named after has been renovated on numerous occasions, and remains the main location the government operates in. The fort is the center of an enormous plot of land, whose extremities are covered by the parliament building, Hall of Ministries and the Jury of Banhockia.

The Jorabores are divided into Northern and Southern islands, and with very low tides, only an occurrence during late Spring, they can become one isle. They're infamous for having a small population which strongly identifies with the isles, which are very flat and susceptible to extremely dry seasons. Either way, many famous figures hail from these islands, including former president Habel Samaba (2018-2023) and businessman Tekkor Gulimol. The largest town on the Jorabores, which only contain around 8 thousand residents, is Oletapa, comprising about a third of those people.

Lastly, Ermanhol and Taakarsu are often grouped together, as they share a lot of geologic history. They're both covered in smooth terrain, replenished with rivers (which often freeze) and are mainly colonies for resource extraction since they're the only isles in which wild, unique species are truly prevalent, alongside the kinds of salt which are found exclusively in this area. Neither of them have settlements reaching above 3 thousand residents, though they do operate separately and have extensive infrastructure systems. Their largest cities are Borelsberg and Acharel respectively.

On one final note, there is a commonly quoted segment in Banhock literature, which remarks about the nature of Banhockia's discovery and history. A paragraph written by Ibanei Solesya, a Elseyr-born, Banhock author whose obsession with the nation was picked apart in a play he wrote, one he never got to see put in motion: [i]"They'd been able to see the horizon for hours in their hike back down the mountain. Upon the earth lay a number of small homes, all roofed with a similar red-tinted wood. The land, an amazing brown and green, and the sea, there couldn't be a more luscious blue than that of the sea. The amalgamation of all the colors was seen in the sky, a mirror, showing where they'd gotten. That wasn't new to them; as beautiful as it was. The sunset that came was slowly turning all those pigments into a blind, pure darkness. The dusk signaled the end of their adventure. But what Datia thought wasn't about the death of the color, rather, about how it served its purpose, it guided her and her partner to the bottom, and from there on, the direction of the hike was on them. It looked like only safety had been bestowed, but in truth, as the moon rose in the sun's mighty spot, Datia understood that it wasn't a full darkening, instead, there was simply a new light."[/i]

The story of the first year of Banhockia has been studied endlessly by economists, psychologists and alike, as they tried to comprehend how the minute group of people that originally stumbled upon the island managed to dig themselves out of the rut they'd fallen into, but also how a local system of governance was so quickly enabled, even if unwillingly by most of the people involved in the new society, and the way that, despite the likely disillusionment with the establishment, people fell back in line so quickly. Currency was more valuable as a commodity than as an economic tool; services were unable to simply be sold, for nothing was worth the work nor was there enough time for most to assist others. Individualism reigned for a moment, and as much as the newly formed government's intervention may have calmed this, the problems persisted.

Documentation of the events were mostly from elitist perspectives, and modern historians notice an elevated distaste towards the majority as time and society progressed, sensing their grip loosening simultaneous to the expansion of towns. The majority, living in a couple of isolated communities in Amalgade and later Marmella, were largely disconnected from the administration, and as such, their lives were generally a lot less restricted; even with the contemporary conditions. Despite this meaning that the relationship between the government and its people was strained, the villages that sprung up in the meantime, probably consisting of some 50 people each, effectively collaborated with each other to make efficient transport networks (mainly on the northern seaboard), island-spanning guilds and small and unappealing, yet existing and useful living spaces in the westerly hills of the island, protecting from the strong winds in the upcoming winter.

A year after the arrival of the expedition, a census was carried out and determined that there were now 496 people in the islands. This statistic came prior to a population increase caused by the discovery of Marmella, allowing the planting of some crops and thus providing nourishment to a larger sector of the population, allowing the production of many offspring. Lots of the newborns died in their infancy, as the third-year census, in 1569, counted 773 people in total. It is very possible that many more babies had been born in the previous two years, but simply died due to the tenuous situation.

Once the populace on Marmella began to develop the island, the government, now led by Halga Masoro as "Supreme Councilor", sought to move their operations to the island, as its wealth-retaining, authoritative status waned with the effectively complete abandonment of currency and overall independence of the people. However, once the administration seized properties at the source and mouth of the Caeselga river (Marmella's main, transversal waterway), taking control of its valuable waters, not using a justification other than [i]"the necessity of egalitarian distribution of aliment"[/i] (Javai Soungre, 1571) there was an immediate sense of distrust cultivated between it and its subjects. As such, in 1574, when the government had begun to build a settlement, fully purposed for its own needs, utilizing much of the valuable material found throughout the waterway, a revolt was staged by enraged civilians who assassinated and kidnapped several politicians. A year later, the construction was completed and the authoritarian regime was fully ousted and replaced by a rotational system, whereby a council made up of guild leaders from every town (of which there were ~6 major ones by this point, major meaning >100 people) would decide on one guild leader (not necessarily in the council) to be the main administrator for one year. The council was refreshed every 2 years, in a selection that was done by local town councils, which would be the main providers of services, a concept truly reintroduced to the economy only after the disappearance of the previous government.

By 1600, with yearly census, there were around 2500 people on the islands. By this point, 6 of the landmasses had been found, the previously named ones alongside Taakarsu island and the Jorabore isles. The final island to be found, Ermanban, the southernmost and third-least populated today, was discovered in 1618, quite a while after the original arrival on the Banhock archipelago.

Each of the isles now plays a role in the Banhockia, now a presidential republic. Marmella, outside of being the main population center with the two most populated cities, is also the produce and trading capital of the nation. Sitting on it are the cities of Deumibla and Enmanhol, the former being larger due to its location, providing it with clean water and better soil, while Enmanhol became the commerce and financial hub, housing many flourishing businesses and the largest port in the nation. Marmella is also the most tourism-friendly spot, with great scenery at almost any time of year.

The first of all of them to be discovered, Amalgade, is undoubtedly the best site for history in the nation. The oldest remnants of the oldest times of Banhockia, while also thriving due to its rare platinum and quartz variants, which is later used elsewhere in the country to produce technological devices and more. Amalgade's largest city is Mesaega, the third-largest in Banhockia.

Bemetha is largely still the capital's island. No other cities exist on it, and the capital itself only has about 1 thousand people on it, mostly civil servants. The fort which the capital is named after has been renovated on numerous occasions, and remains the main location the government operates in. The fort is the center of an enormous plot of land, whose extremities are covered by the parliament building, Hall of Ministries and the Jury of Banhockia.

The Jorabores are divided into Northern and Southern islands, and with very low tides, only an occurrence during late Spring, they can become one isle. They're infamous for having a small population which strongly identifies with the isles, which are very flat and susceptible to extremely dry seasons. Either way, many famous figures hail from these islands, including former president Habel Samaba (2018-2023) and businessman Tekkor Gulimol. The largest town on the Jorabores, which only contain around 8 thousand residents, is Oletapa, comprising about a third of those people.

Lastly, Ermanhol and Taakarsu are often grouped together, as they share a lot of geologic history. They're both covered in smooth terrain, replenished with rivers (which often freeze) and are mainly colonies for resource extraction since they're the only isles in which wild, unique species are truly prevalent, alongside the kinds of salt which are found exclusively in this area. Neither of them have settlements reaching above 3 thousand residents, though they do operate separately and have extensive infrastructure systems. Their largest cities are Borelsberg and Acharel respectively.

On one final note, there is a commonly quoted segment in Banhock literature, which remarks about the nature of Banhockia's discovery and history. A paragraph written by Ibanei Solesya, a Elseyr-born, Banhock author whose obsession with the nation was picked apart in a play he wrote, one he never got to see put in motion: [i]"They'd been able to see the horizon for hours in their hike back down the mountain. Upon the earth lay a number of small homes, all roofed with a similar red-tinted wood. The land, an amazing brown and green, and the sea, there couldn't be a more luscious blue than that of the sea. The amalgamation of all the colors was seen in the sky, a mirror, showing where they'd gotten. That wasn't new to them; as beautiful as it was. The sunset that came was slowly turning all those pigments into a blind, pure darkness. The dusk signaled the end of their adventure. But what Datia thought wasn't about the death of the color, rather, about how it served its purpose, it guided her and her partner to the bottom, and from there on, the direction of the hike was on them. It looked like only safety had been bestowed, but in truth, as the moon rose in the sun's mighty spot, Datia understood that it wasn't a full darkening, instead, there was simply a new light."[/i]
